2026-11-07-video.caption:
What ISO really changes

At fixed aperture and shutter duration, increasing ISO usually brightens the rendered image. It does not add captured light. Noise depends on exposure and the camera's design and processing.

• Captured light: Set by the scene, aperture and duration.
• ISO setting: Influences gain and image rendering.
• Practical choice: Balance exposure, motion and noise.

Focal length and your frame

For the same sensor size, a shorter focal length gives a wider angle of view; a longer focal length narrows it. Perspective also depends on where you place the camera.

• Shorter lens: Includes a wider view on the same sensor.
• Longer lens: Narrows the view on the same sensor.
• Camera position: Moving the camera changes perspective.
